plausible_interpretation_differences: The human FG4 set is {A.2, B.3, B.4, C.1, C.3, D}. All three demographics-only runs assert A.1 (two also assert B.2). Both sides therefore code within parent theme A, but at ADJACENT subthemes — A.2 on the human side, A.1 on the synthetic side. Subtheme-level overlap is 0 while parent-theme-level overlap is not.
This is a difference in WHICH subtheme was expressed, not evidence that the synthetic groups produced nothing: every run returned quote-verified codes with reach 1.0.
The enriched runs for the same FG do share codes with the human set (3, 1 and 1 shared), so this human coding is reachable in principle under another condition.
Whether A.1 vs A.2 reflects a genuine stance difference or a coding boundary question requires a human reading both transcripts. No causal claim is made here.

parent_theme_level_note.parent_theme_overlap: non-zero (theme A present on both sides)

correction: An earlier phrasing said the human coding 'centres on B/C-family subthemes' and the synthetic runs assert 'A-family only'. That was imprecise: the human set includes A.2. The accurate statement is that both sides code within theme A at different subthemes.
